stories.title: Introducing Muse Glimmer
stories.paragraph: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weights model licensed under Apache 2.0, marking a departure from the company's previous Llama license terms. The model is positioned for agentic use cases, with Meta claiming strong performance on end-to-end full-task benchmarks. The Apache 2.0 license removes many of the commercial and redistribution restrictions that had complicated earlier Llama deployments.

stories.title: I was accused of using AI in my dissertation but I wrote it all myself
stories.paragraph: A student reported being accused of using AI to write their dissertation despite having written it entirely themselves, highlighting the reliability problems with AI detection tools used in academic settings. The case illustrates a growing tension in universities that have adopted AI detection software without a clear consensus on its accuracy or fairness as a basis for disciplinary action. False positives from such tools can carry serious academic consequences, raising questions about due process when institutions act on algorithmic outputs.

stories.title: How Claude marks AI-generated content
stories.paragraph: Anthropic has published documentation explaining how Claude labels or signals AI-generated content in its outputs. The support article details the methods Claude uses to indicate when text has been produced by the model, a practice relevant to ongoing debates about transparency and disclosure in AI-assisted writing. The guidance is notable as institutions and platforms increasingly seek technical standards for distinguishing human from machine-generated content.

stories.title: Font looks perfectly normal to humans but wreaks havoc on AI
stories.paragraph: Researchers have developed a font that appears visually standard to human readers but systematically confuses AI text-recognition and language models. The technique exploits differences between how humans and neural networks process visual letterforms, effectively acting as an adversarial input at the typographic level. The work contributes to a broader body of adversarial machine-learning research that probes the gap between human and model perception.

stories.title: The AI Slop Backlash Is Having an Impact
stories.paragraph: Wired reports that public and creator pushback against low-quality AI-generated content — often called "AI slop" — is beginning to influence platform policies and brand behavior. Advertisers and publishers have started pulling or labeling AI-generated material in response to audience complaints and declining engagement metrics. The piece argues that consumer pressure is functioning as a market signal in the absence of comprehensive regulatory standards for AI content quality.

stories.title: As AI eats the web, the internet's collective memory is disappearing
stories.paragraph: The Walrus argues that the proliferation of AI-generated content is degrading the quality of web search results and eroding the web's function as a searchable archive of human knowledge. The piece connects the decline of Google Search's usefulness to the flood of algorithmically produced pages that optimize for ranking rather than informational value. It raises the concern that as AI-written content displaces original sources, the training data for future models — and the record of past events — becomes increasingly unreliable.

stories.title: I'm not anti-AI, but I have QUALLMS
stories.paragraph: A blogger has coined the term QUALLMS — an acronym — to articulate a set of specific, structured concerns about large language models that fall short of outright opposition to the technology. The post attempts to move the discourse beyond binary pro- or anti-AI positions by naming distinct categories of critique such as quality, accuracy, labor, and legal issues. It is notable for trying to provide a vocabulary for nuanced criticism in a public conversation that often collapses into camps.

stories.title: Tech leaders say AI means less work; staff say they work up to 90 hours a week
stories.paragraph: A BBC report documents a disconnect between technology executives' claims that AI reduces workloads and the reported experience of employees, some of whom say they are working up to 90 hours per week. The gap suggests that productivity gains attributed to AI tools may not be translating into reduced demands on workers, and may instead be raising output expectations. The findings are relevant to ongoing debates about how AI-driven efficiency is distributed between employers and employees.

stories.title: The Water Footprint of AI
stories.paragraph: A peer-reviewed study published in Water Research quantifies the water consumption associated with AI model training and inference, adding to a growing literature on the environmental costs of large-scale compute. Data centers used for AI workloads require significant volumes of water for cooling, and the paper provides estimates that make the scale of this consumption concrete. The research is relevant for policymakers and companies assessing the sustainability profile of AI deployments alongside energy and carbon metrics.

stories.title: Nvidia is pulling Wall Street into the AI buildout
stories.paragraph: Nvidia is reportedly involved in structuring a $500 billion funding package that would draw financial institutions into financing AI infrastructure at scale. The arrangement would connect Wall Street capital directly to the buildout of data centers and compute capacity needed to run large AI systems. If completed, the deal would represent one of the largest coordinated private investments in AI infrastructure to date.

stories.title: Show HN: AI Pulse a fake LED strip beside the macOS Dock that shows agent status
stories.paragraph: A developer has released AI Pulse, a macOS utility that renders a simulated LED strip alongside the Dock to display the real-time status of Claude Code agent sessions running in parallel. The tool was built to solve a practical problem: the developer was losing time by switching between windows to check whether agents were idle, running, or waiting on a permission prompt. The project is open source on GitHub and was inspired by a hardware peripheral called SidePulse.io.

stories.title: Zuckerberg's superyacht ignored emergency channel, failed to aid stranded boat
stories.paragraph: Ars Technica reports that a superyacht owned by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg allegedly failed to respond on a maritime emergency channel while a nearby boat was in distress. The incident is governed by maritime law, which generally requires vessels to render assistance to those in peril at sea when it can be done without serious danger. The story has drawn attention partly because of Zuckerberg's prominent public profile and the timing relative to Meta's ongoing AI and technology initiatives.

stories.title: AI Boot Camps Surge as Workers Race to Learn New Skills
stories.paragraph: Demand for short-form AI training programs has risen sharply, prompting colleges and private providers to expand credential offerings aimed at working professionals seeking to add AI skills. The trend reflects employer pressure on existing staff to become proficient with AI tools, rather than solely hiring new graduates. Boot camps and certificate programs, which typically run weeks to a few months rather than the years required for a degree, have become a practical option for workers looking to retool quickly.

stories.title: Beyond Naturalness: Probing Automated Text-To-Speech Evaluators on Linguistically Grounded Dimensions
stories.paragraph: Researchers have examined how well automated TTS evaluation methods — specifically Mean Opinion Score (MOS) predictors and Audio Large Language Model judges — align with human perception of speech quality. Rather than treating 'naturalness' as a single scalar, the study deconstructs it into 10 distinct perceptual dimensions derived from a linguistically grounded annotation schema. The work addresses a gap in the field: automated evaluators are widely used as proxies for human judgment, but their fidelity across specific perceptual axes had not been systematically tested. The findings have direct implications for how TTS systems are benchmarked and compared.

stories.title: From Values to Benchmarks: Evaluating Large Language Models for Governmental Use in Dutch
stories.paragraph: A research team has developed the 'Grip on LLMs' framework, an evaluation suite for assessing large language models in Dutch governmental contexts, created in collaboration with domain experts from a major Dutch municipality. Most existing LLM benchmarks are designed for English and do not account for the specific values of public administration, such as transparency, accountability, and accuracy in policy-relevant language. The framework jointly addresses linguistic requirements and institutional values, filling a gap for non-English public sector deployments. Its development with practitioners rather than solely in academia is intended to ensure the criteria reflect real operational needs.

stories.title: Decoding-Level Taboo: A Diagnostic Stress Test for LLM Robustness
stories.paragraph: Researchers propose a diagnostic framework called Decoding-Level Taboo designed to stress-test LLM robustness under constrained generation conditions that deviate from standard benchmark settings. The core observation is that real-world deployments impose structural constraints — such as complex system prompts and safety guardrails — that push models off the narrow generation path for which they are optimized, causing performance to diverge from benchmark scores. By systematically restricting decoding choices, the test exposes brittleness that nominal evaluations obscure. The work highlights a mismatch between controlled benchmark performance and practical reliability.

stories.title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling
stories.paragraph: This paper addresses verifier-free test-time scaling (VF-TTS), a method for improving LLM reasoning at inference time without relying on external verifiers such as compilers or trained value functions. The authors introduce 'consilience' as a guiding principle — selecting outputs based on convergent evidence across multiple rollouts rather than external validation signals. VF-TTS has attracted attention precisely because high-quality verifiers are unavailable for many reasoning tasks, making internal consistency a practical alternative. The approach is notable for extending test-time compute methods to domains where ground-truth checking is not feasible.

stories.title: Fusion Training for Mathematical Generalization in Large Language Models
stories.paragraph: Researchers present a systematic study of Thinking Mode Fusion (TMF), a training approach that combines a concise non-thinking mode and a long-form chain-of-thought thinking mode within a single LLM. The study focuses specifically on mathematical generalization and examines two previously underexplored variables: the ratio of training data from each mode and the schedule used to alternate between them during training. Prior work established TMF as a viable architecture but left its training dynamics largely uncharacterized. The results offer concrete guidance for practitioners training models that need to support both rapid and deliberate reasoning styles.

theme: Research Papers: Novel Model Architectures & Methods

stories.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
stories.paragraph: Researchers propose a 'model diffing' technique for identifying which internal features in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are introduced or altered by multimodal training, as opposed to being inherited from a text-only base model. The method builds on sparse autoencoders (SAEs), which decompose hidden states into interpretable feature directions, but extends this to isolate changes attributable specifically to visual training. Existing SAE-based approaches can inspect hidden states post-hoc but do not readily distinguish multimodal-specific features from pre-existing ones. The work aims to make MLLM internals more auditable and to enable targeted behavioral control.

stories.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
stories.paragraph: The paper introduces BDH-CQ, a reasoning model that processes inference-time inputs by continuously updating a recurrent memory and then solving queries through iterative computation in a high-dimensional latent space, without generating explicit intermediate reasoning steps. This contrasts with chain-of-thought approaches, which verbalize reasoning in natural language tokens. The model is evaluated on the public ARC-AGI-1 benchmark, providing a concrete point of comparison against other reasoning systems. The recurrent latent mechanism is designed to decouple reasoning depth from output token length.

theme: Research Papers: AI in Specialized Domains

stories.title: GENCO - A Unified Neural Solver Embedded in a Development Framework for Steady-State Grid Analysis
stories.paragraph: Researchers present GENCO (GEometric Neural Corrective Optimizer), a neural solver designed for steady-state transmission grid analysis that handles both power flow (PF) and optimal power flow (OPF) problems while enforcing physical consistency constraints. Foundation models have seen limited adoption in engineering domains precisely because they do not inherently respect domain-specific physical laws, making GENCO's constraint-aware architecture a distinguishing feature. The solver is embedded in a development framework intended to make it accessible to power systems engineers without deep machine learning expertise. The work addresses a practical gap between general-purpose AI progress and engineering-domain requirements.

stories.title: Space-Creating versus Dead Possession: An Off-Ball Possession-Quality Index for Broadcast Football
stories.paragraph: Researchers introduce an off-ball possession-quality index for football (soccer) that distinguishes between possession sequences that create space and those that do not, addressing a known limitation of raw possession percentage statistics. Existing event-based frameworks such as expected threat, VAEP, and on-ball value assign scores only to on-ball actions, leaving the spatial and tactical value of off-ball circulation unmeasured. The index is designed to work with broadcast footage rather than requiring tracking data, broadening its practical applicability. The work formalizes the intuition that 60% possession recycled in one's own half carries different strategic value than 60% spent in the opponent's half.

stories.title: DSLE: A Learning Environment for Dark Souls Boss Encounters
stories.paragraph: The Dark Souls Learning Environment (DSLE) is a containerized platform that exposes all 22 boss encounters from Dark Souls: Remastered as reinforcement learning benchmarks via a Gymnasium-style interface. Each environment step corresponds to a real action executed against the running game, creating conditions with high-dimensional visual input, real-time combat dynamics, and sparse terminal rewards. These properties are intended to challenge agent capabilities in ways that more stylized RL benchmarks do not. The platform is positioned as a test bed for agents that must handle partial observability and long-horizon planning without dense reward shaping.

stories.title: Fairness in Link Prediction Beyond Demographic Parity: A Reproducibility Study
stories.paragraph: This reproducibility study reexamines the claim by Mattos et al. (2025) that demographic parity (ΔDP), a standard fairness metric in link prediction, fails to detect exposure bias in ranked outputs because it ignores the position at which links appear in rankings. The authors confirm that ΔDP can show aggregate parity even when links for specific subgroup pairs are systematically ranked lower than others, validating the original critique. The study goes further by testing alternative fairness metrics that are sensitive to ranking position, providing a more complete picture of bias in link prediction systems. The work contributes to an ongoing debate about which fairness criteria are appropriate for graph-based recommendation and social network analysis tasks.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders Writes Letter to Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Mark Zuckerberg
stories.paragraph: U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders sent a letter to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg calling for a pause on certain AI development activities. The letter represents a notable instance of a senior elected official directly addressing the heads of three of the most prominent AI companies by name, and reflects growing congressional interest in AI governance. While the specific demands and framing in the letter center on concerns about labor displacement and concentration of power, the direct correspondence format signals an escalation from general legislative discussion to targeted executive outreach. No legislative action was attached to the letter at the time of publication.
